Hi Kimberly —

Thanks for the quick kickoff yesterday. I pulled together a few artifacts the implementation team asked for so your sizing can be more concrete: attached is a 48-hour sample of anonymized request metadata (arcadia_sample_traffic.csv) and three prompt examples that reflect our triage + summarization flow. A few clarifications from our side:

- Typical request size (tokens in): ~350 tokens average, but the triage path is often short (~120 tokens).
- Context needs: around 60% of requests need access to 6k–8k tokens (patient notes + recent message history).
- Peak concurrency: our beta expects spikes to 120 qps for short bursts (5–10m) and sustained 20–30 qps baseline.
- Latency SLO: 300ms p50 for triage responses; 800ms p50 acceptable for full summaries.
- Compliance/residency: production must stay in us-east-1 and meet SOC2 controls; we can share our procurement contact for security docs.

Please let us know what you need to finalize a model shortlist and an initial capacity recommendation for a 30-day pilot.

Best,
Elena

Elena — thanks for the sample, this is exactly what we need. Looping in Grace (modeling) and Dylan (capacity) to run a quick pass. Initial asks from our side to make the shortlist crisp:

- Confirm percent of queries that absolutely need the 8k window vs those that could work with a 2k window as fallback.
- Can you share the 30-day expected monthly token volume estimate (or a good guess) so we can size batching and reserved capacity math?

Prelim thoughts (we'll validate against the CSV):
- Lane A (low-latency, on-prem/dedicated): 7B quantized (INT8/4) with aggressive caching; target p50 <300ms for triage.
- Lane B (balanced, dedicated): 13B INT4 with KV caching for the 6–8k windows — recommended for the pilot.
- Lane C (high-fidelity fallback, hosted): 70B float/amp with larger context when summaries require it.

I've attached an initial-sizing-sheet.xlsx that has template fields for avg tokens, peak qps, and a draft cost sketch. Grace/Dylan — can you review and drop lane-specific token assumptions and a suggested pilot capacity (reserved GPUs + burst policy) by end of day tomorrow?

Thanks Kim — I reviewed the CSV and highlighted a few workload patterns: high short-query volume (helpful for batching) and a long-tail of large-context requests that correlate with 1:1 patient conversations. Quick notes:

- Model lane proposals (details):
  * Lane A — Low-latency: 7B quantized (Q4_0 / INT8 pipeline). Typical payload 120–350 tokens in, and we expect p50 around 200–320ms with continuous batching disabled for critical triage paths. Good for high qps short flows.
  * Lane B — Balanced (recommended pilot): 13B INT4 with 8k context support through segmented KV caching; expect 1.6–2.3k tokens generated on average for summaries. A single P4d-equivalent node pool (4-8 GPUs) with dedicated prefix cache should cover baseline 30 qps and absorb short spikes to ~100 qps with autoscale/burst.
  * Lane C — High-fidelity fallback: 70B hosted model (float/amp) for the heaviest summaries and escalations — used <5% of traffic but critical for accuracy.

- Token-volume sketch (monthly, rough):
  * Baseline monthly requests: 1.2M
  * Avg tokens/request (in+out): 1,100 -> ~1.32B tokens/mo
  * If 60% of requests use 6–8k context, tokens jump to ~1.9B tokens/mo (worst-case).

- Ops notes: prefix/KV cache hit rate expected to reduce per-request compute by ~35% on Lane B. We'll model the effect in the sizing sheet.

I've uploaded a short calc and a Drive folder with the modeling doc: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2bArcadiaOnboard (see 'modeling_notes_v1').

Grace O'Connor
Senior Systems PM, Modeling — Redwood Inference

Elena — thanks for the pilot volume estimate and SOC2 doc. Action items and summary for clarity:

1) Finalized pilot model lanes (per Arcadia constraints):
   - Lane A (triage, low-latency): 7B quantized — serves ~55% of pilot traffic.
   - Lane B (pilot primary): 13B INT4 with prefix/KV caching — serves ~40% of pilot traffic and supports 6–8k context. Recommended deployment: Redwood Dedicated (reserved pool) in us-east-1 with 4 GPU nodes, burst to 8 for 90-minute hourly spikes; autoscale policy and prefix cache retained across instances.
   - Lane C (fallback): 70B hosted model — used for <5% escalations.

2) Pilot sizing & cost snapshot (30 days, conservative):
